title: Flashing Lights

location.name: The Childhood Window on the Road Winding Down (Baltimere)
location.kind: childhood family house, ground-floor living room with a street-facing window
location.real_analog: a modest brick end-of-row or detached house on a curving, potholed hillside street in inner-ring Baltimore (e.g. Hampden or Woodberry above the Jones Falls valley)
near: the curb where the car pulls up

situation: The adult POET falls or floats in black space with lights flashing while the EX, in distress, floats unreachable; everything stays black as his eyes dilate. The camera goes into and through his eyes into a flashback: Young POET (six) home alone at the living-room window on a winter night watches a car pull up, its headlights sweeping the room over the bumps in the road, his parents arguing inside it. A ghost child appears, hugs him, vanishes, returns and hands him a tambourine, which he throws through the window, shattering it.
time_of_day: night (void: 'after midnight'); flashback is a winter night
weather_light: pitch black void with intermittent flashing lights; flashback: dark room raked by moving headlights, curtains pulled and blinds up, a strangely warm heavy winter breeze (inferred snow outside from spine FL044)

set_pieces.name: Falling with headlights off
set_pieces.what_happens: POET in black space, falling or floating, lights flashing; EX in distress floats nearby, unreachable.
lines: I heard a / scream for help
while falling / with my / headlights / off—
a pending marriage,
a set of walls caving inward
set_pieces.camera: floating wide in a black stage, strobing practicals; EX kept back-to-camera at a fixed unreachable distance
set_pieces.position: the black void continuing below the Out of Life floor-hole

set_pieces.name: Eyes dilate
set_pieces.what_happens: Everything still black; his eyes dilate trying to see, then the camera pushes into and through them into the flashback.
lines: an emergency call / while tossing & turning—
the mirror after midnight
after a day of life / dilated at the sun
I've accepted that we won't / make it.
set_pieces.camera: extreme close-up on the POET's eye, pupil opening, macro push-through into the next scene

set_pieces.name: Car pulls up
set_pieces.what_happens: Young POET at the living-room window watches a car pull up, its lights flashing through the room because of the angle and the bumps in the road.
lines: Heart break revisits / an old scene.
I was six—
I recall, when
set_pieces.camera: from behind the child at the window, headlight beams sweeping across walls and ceiling
set_pieces.position: living-room window, ground floor, facing the street and curb

set_pieces.name: The ghost child
set_pieces.what_happens: A ghost kid appears and hugs Young POET, telling him his parents' marriage won't last, then disappears.
lines: the ghost of a dead / & a love-less / seven-year old child
appeared & shared
that my parents' / marriage wouldn't / last—
set_pieces.camera: soft two-shot at child height, ghost slightly diffused; frost breath on the windowpane insert

set_pieces.name: Parents arguing in the car
set_pieces.what_happens: Ghost gone, Young POET stays at the window watching his parents argue in the car, curtains pulled and blinds up, left home alone.
lines: a child is left / home alone
with curtains / pulled & blinds up
to see / flashing lights
of two souls on / a road winding down
set_pieces.camera: over-the-shoulder through the glass to the lit car interior; reverse close-up on the child's face in headlight wash
set_pieces.position: living-room window looking down to the curb

set_pieces.name: Tambourine through the window
set_pieces.what_happens: The ghost child hands Young POET a tambourine; he throws it through the window, shattering the glass.
lines: and no tears
and no fucks
and no love / to give.
ode to teach.
set_pieces.camera: high-speed glass shatter from outside looking in, tambourine exiting toward camera

arrival.from_previous: He keeps falling from the Out of Life floor-hole into black space; the camera then goes into and through his eyes to reach the childhood window as a flashback.

departure.to_next: The tambourine he throws leaves through the shattered window and tumbles through black space toward the chapel; the POET himself does not travel (he is absent from the next poem).

encoding: The window is the first place the poet ever watched a love end from inside a room, so the adult fall lands him back there: the high-rise window of poem 01 rhymes with the child's street window. The car's lights are the 'flashing lights' and the road 'winding down' is the marriage; throwing the tambourine through the glass is the child breaking the frame he was made to watch through. Inferred: the street-level house is the origin point (map: 'personal origins') beneath the tower he fell from.
